newsitem.title: USA: Hearing set in Hillsborough Cty, Fla, stadium suit.
newsitem.headline: Hearing set in Hillsborough Cty, Fla, stadium suit.

text.p: Hillsborough County Circuit Judge Sam Pendino set a hearing for 1400 EDT Friday on the county's motion to dismiss a lawsuit that could jeopardize bond financing for a $168 football stadium, county officials said Monday.

The Florida county is also considering filing a countersuit against former Tampa Mayor William Poe, who has twice sued to block the use of public funds for the Tampa Bay Bucanners' stadium, said Ben Kelly, an aide to county commission Chairman Jim Norman.
Poe sued in August to block a referendum on the sales tax increase that will back the bonds. The effort failed when Circuit Judge James Whittmore up held the constitutionality of the ballot question.
On Sept 3, voters approved the half-cent sales tax increase that will raise $2.7 billion over 30 years for schools, roads, public safety and the stadium.

Poe sued the county again last week, saying Whittmore had been legally barred from considering the stadium issue separately from the other projects to be funded with tax money. He said the project would unconstitutionally use public money for a project that will mainly benefit a private, for-profit team.
County Attorney Emeline Acton filed a motion to dismiss Poe's suit on grounds that it raised no new issues.

Acton also recommended that the county countersue Poe on charges of interfereing with the county's business and contractual relationship with the Bucs. Kelly said a decision was still pending on whether to proceed with the countersuit.

Acton and other county officials were in a meeting Monday to determine whether the bond sale could proceed while legal action was pending. The bonds are to be sold in late October or early November via Smith Barney Inc.
"We have to start the groundbreaking soon and we want to make sure that everything is done on time," Kelly said.
